conditions.name: nominal
conditions.description: Block starts at the fixed nominal pose (x=0.50 m, y=-0.15 m, yaw 0) on the table; default light, table and floor colors, no occlusion.

conditions.name: object_position
conditions.description: Block start (x, y) = nominal + a seeded uniform offset, each axis within +/-0.04 m (yaw stays 0). Changes the block pose the state-based controller reads. Bounded and reproducible per seed.

conditions.name: lighting
conditions.description: Rendered-image light only: seeded light direction (azimuth within +/-80 deg of nominal) and diffuse/ambient intensity scale in [0.3, 1.0]. Physics and controller state are unchanged; a scripted state-based controller is not expected to react. No claim about learned-policy robustness.

conditions.name: background
conditions.description: Rendered-image only: table and floor RGB colors perturbed by a seeded delta within +/-0.35 per channel (clipped to [0,1]). Physics unchanged; a scripted state-based controller is not expected to react. No claim about learned-policy robustness.

conditions.name: occlusion
conditions.description: A gray rectangular patch (side fraction of the 320x240 frame in [0.10, 0.25], seeded position) is painted over the RENDERED image only; the simulator state and the scripted controller are unchanged. A scripted state-based controller is not expected to react. No claim about learned-policy robustness.

denominator_definitions.planned: all trials given (never-attempted trials stay here)
denominator_definitions.infra_abort_rate: attempted trials terminated by an infra reason / attempted
denominator_definitions.artifact_completeness: present+hash-recorded / expected (expected includes video+trace per attempt)

failures.note: Every trial appears in exactly one row. infra/abort trials stay unscored and are never counted as task failures; task failures are completed trials scored failure.

comparisons.caveat: The exact McNemar p-value uses only discordant pairs. With the small n typical here it does not support significance claims: it assumes independent pairs, a fixed paired design, and a pre-specified test, and ignores multiple comparisons across conditions. Treat differences as descriptive.

limitations: The controllers evaluated by this repository are scripted, state-based programs reading simulator state; they are not learned policies and not trained checkpoints.
Simulation results use a PyBullet Panda arm with rendered simulator frames. This is not the SO-101 arm and not physical hardware; no conclusion about real-robot performance follows.
Mock-provenance results are seeded fixtures and are never evidence of robotics performance.
Visual-only conditions (lighting, background, occlusion) do not change what a state-based controller reads; they say nothing about the visual robustness of a learned policy.
Small sample sizes: Wilson intervals are wide and any difference between controllers is descriptive. p-values from so few discordant pairs do not support significance claims.
Scoring agreement between independent human scorers and reset-time improvements are not measured by this report; they need independent human measurement (see docs/evaluation-protocol.md).
